note: Clean pass with caveats. CODE DERIVATION: core-model pattern 1 -- the processing script melts ITEM_COLS=['Q1'..'Q15'] by name, so the IRW item code IS the S5 column name. LEVEL 1 CHECKED: the S5 .xlsx is an SPSS export with bare headers (Q1..Q15) and no variable or value labels; the study's S6 coding manual labels each column 'NEP Scale Question k' (coding 'Numeric Value, 999=missing'), and the S1 File prints statement k numbered 1..15. So Qk -> statement k is a label match through the study's own coding manual, not an order inference; mapping_basis=paper_explicit because the wording is in a supplement rather than the data file. TEXT: all 15 statements, the instructions sentence and the option legend transcribed verbatim from S1 File (pdftotext of a text PDF, not OCR); line wraps joined. Kept literally: the instruction's 'mostly closely align' (sic), item 4's 'ensure' and 'unliveable' (Dunlap et al. 2000 print 'insure' and 'unlivable' -- the study's own wording ships, not the canonical), the capitalised 'NOT', and the curly single quotes around 'ecological crisis'. OPTIONS: the form's tick columns are headed SA/A/N/D/SD and the legend expands them as 'SA - strongly agree', 'A - agree', 'N - neutral', 'D - disagree', 'SD - strongly disagree'; option_text ships the legend's lower-case expansions without the abbreviations. OPTION->RESP DIRECTION, the substantive decision: the stored values are SCORED, not raw. Paper Methods and S1 File p.2: odd items SA=5..SD=1, even items SA=1..SD=5. So option_text is mapped per item -- odd items resp 5='strongly agree'; even items resp 1='strongly agree', resp 5='strongly disagree'. Verified (verify_singleton_2021_carbon_reduction.R, PASS): live per-person sum of Q1..Q15 equals S5 NEP_Tot for 106/106; published total M/SD/alpha reproduce exactly from the stored values (combined 54.40/6.57/0.787, Australia 54.58/6.91/0.815, UK 54.10/6.04/0.734) and fail badly if the seven even items are re-reversed (49.91/3.80/0.223); flipping any single item lowers combined alpha (0.66-0.78 vs 0.787). STEP 3b: instrument matches -- 15 items, 1-5, odd/even NEP alternation, and NEP_Tot is exactly their sum. But the IRW dictionary Description ('Pro-environmental-behavior scale, hospital pharmacy staff, 15 items') misnames it: this is the revised New Ecological Paradigm scale, an environmental-attitude/worldview measure, not a behaviour scale; the instrument field names the NEP. RIGHTS: register has no NEP row. No restriction found or quotable -- the S1 File carries no terms, and a web search for Dunlap NEP permission/copyright terms returned no licence, fee, permission or redistribution statement; the wording was copied from a CC BY 4.0 supplement. Silence is permission under the quote test. Per the 2026-09-10 rule no register row was written (a round may not write ship). Precedent: liem_2024_attitude_env (batch_078) shipped NEP wording on the same basis. LANGUAGE: English (Australian and UK hospital pharmacies); no language/_translated columns. correct_response blank (attitude scale); single trivial section_id; no section_prompt. RETRY TEST: n/a -- written.
public_note: The seven even-numbered items (Q2, Q4, Q6, Q8, Q10, Q12, Q14) are the NEP's anti-ecological statements and are stored already reverse-scored as the study scored them, so for those items resp=1 is 'strongly agree' and resp=5 is 'strongly disagree' (the option_text rows are mapped accordingly); for odd-numbered items resp=5 is 'strongly agree', so higher resp means a more pro-ecological response on every item.

note: MAPPING (paper_order): nothing in the study ties gad1..gad7 to text.
